answer: Yes. Nell’s movement from underpaid cashier to wealthy daughter-in-law and back to voluntary cashier work creates a coherent arc about dignity, belonging, and autonomy. Miss Emily’s generosity and controlling instincts drive that conflict, while recurring details—the name tag, wages, ledgers, and ownership—connect the scenes thematically. The ending offers a satisfying resolution: Nell accepts her changed circumstances without surrendering the work she considers her own.
